Unnecessary temporary

`core` is meant to be self-contained, dependencies on module code are not allowed in theory.

So if this general approach is approved, this would likely need to be done through a new method in `Script`, which can then be implemented in `GDScript`.

I think the complexity required and the module dependency might be an indication that it's a potentially fragile thing to support this with built-in scripts, they're a bit of a house of cards as it is, might be a limitation better documented than solved unless it can be done more flexibly

I think it might be better to take an approach where the resource loader calls some method on all the resources it holds to query this instead, that'd help other cases as well

Alternatively the `get_classes_used()` method could call `ResourceLoader::get_classes_used()` for each built-in resource path. Then it could be automatically handled by GDScript format loader (it will need some tweaks to handle built-in script paths).

@KoBeWi The problem is that this solution would require to load each sub-resource in every scene scan, making the project detecting process even longer, when we just need to get the source code of scripts for parsing. This is too much for a corner case.
Also, `ResourceLoader::get_classes_used()` relies on path extensions to recognize the appropriate loaders. It wouldn't be able to identify those with how built-in paths are structured.

> The problem is that this solution would require to load each sub-resource in every scene scan, making the project detecting process even longer

I guess https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8750 would alleviate that (it proposes adding a way to extract sub-resources without loading the whole file).

Although build profile generation is not something that you have to do often, no? Making it longer shouldn't be a big problem then. Like, the upgrade tool opens all scenes and the project _and saves them_, and it takes like 20 minutes max in big projects, so it's not terrible (again, unless you do it often).

> It wouldn't be able to identify those with how built-in paths are structured.

In most cases the will have `::GDScript` part, so it can be used to recognize them.
Already, I changed the logic to make use of `ResourceLoader::get_classes_used()` instead. Doing away with the GDScript dependency.
